requirements.requirement: Publish the staged public tree anonymously at /public/ on TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Direct requests returned HTTP 200 with content byte-identical to the staged public page. Apache was observed listening on 8080 before and after restart, with no port-80 listener in the final executor check.

requirements.requirement: Publish /staff/ using HTTP Basic authentication for reader with the demonstration password, while keeping staff content inaccessible after missing or failed authentication.
requirements.summary: Anonymous and incorrect-credential requests to the staff index and roster returned 401 and did not match protected content. The supplied reader credentials returned HTTP 200 with byte-identical staged files, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Do not serve the password files or directory listings.
requirements.summary: Bounded protected-path probes completed successfully only for 403/404 responses, and listing probes did not return an Apache directory index. The effective configuration applies Options -Indexes, denies the default document root, and keeps both credential files restrictively permissioned.

requirements.requirement: Keep the supplied pages under /srv/legacy2/web-authentication-boundary intact.
requirements.summary: Final SHA-256 hashes for all public and staff files equal the preparation baseline, and served authenticated/anonymous copies match those source files.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained Ubuntu 16.04.7 with kernel 4.4.0-210-generic. Apache 2.4.18 from the Xenial repositories was installed and remained operational after reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Public and authenticated staff content behaved correctly on port 8080, protected resources and directory listings remained inaccessible, source pages stayed intact, and the legacy OS/kernel were retained. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed coherently and cross-checked by the lifecycle boot identities.
limitations: Credential-related evidence redaction obscures some literal protected-path status values and final credential-file mode text, although the successful command assertions accepted only 403/404 responses and directly verified authentication behavior.

The fixed after-executor listening-socket snapshot is empty despite executor checks showing Apache on 8080 shortly before and after restart. This unexplained inconsistency modestly lowers confidence, though repeated HTTP and listener checks directly support service availability.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Apache installation, credential-file generation, site configuration, enablement, and restart were causally necessary for the requested service. The node reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol. Temporary validation directories were trap-cleaned, and the installation log did not remain after reboot. Final observations show no failed services or damaged package state. The protocol itself was strong: healthy pre-restart service and HTTP state, restart acknowledgement and bounded unavailability, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and full post-restart service/content/authentication recovery.
